findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but its body is just `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler declares abstract `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, none of which are implemented. Instantiating it (which `Detector.detector_handler` does via `group_type.detector_handler(self)`) raises TypeError. Before this change, `evaluate` returned an empty list, so the metric alert detector was safe to construct. Any detector of type `metric_alert_fire` will now crash in `process_detectors`.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The docstring of StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate says it 'returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`', but the method now returns a dict keyed by group key. Callers relying on the docstring will iterate keys or call list methods and get errors.

findings.title: Duplicate group keys are now silently overwritten before any occurrence is produced
findings.body: In `evaluate`, `results[result.group_key] = result` overwrites any earlier result with the same group key. The removed code in process_detectors logged an error on duplicates. Now the first result is dropped silently, with no log or metric, and its occurrence is never produced. The dict removes duplicates by construction, but the loss is no longer observable.

findings.title: Mock occurrence builder ignores `value`, so tests can't catch wrong values
findings.body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` never uses the `value` argument. Tests such as `test_results_on_change` and `test_dedupe` pass `6` as the value while the evaluated input is `100` or `8`, and the assertions still pass. The tests therefore don't verify that the hook receives and uses the actual group value, which is the core of the new hook.
